title: International society of sports nutrition position stand: caffeine and exercise performance (Guest et al. 2021)
content: Guest NS et al., Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition 2021 — Caffeine (roughly 3-6 mg/kg bodyweight, taken ~60 minutes before exercise) can improve endurance performance, and to a lesser/more variable extent strength/power performance, for many individuals. Response to caffeine varies substantially between individuals due to genetic factors (e.g. CYP1A2 metabolism) and habitual intake/tolerance.

title: International society of sports nutrition position stand: caffeine and exercise performance (Guest et al. 2021)
content: ISSN Caffeine 2021 — Caffeine can negatively affect sleep quality (especially if taken later in the day), and can increase heart rate/anxiety in sensitive individuals; interactions with certain medications and cardiovascular conditions are a real concern. Product implication: caffeine guidance must ask about sensitivity, sleep habits, anxiety, cardiovascular history, and current medications before suggesting a dose, must never suggest a high/aggressive dose, and should note timing relative to sleep — this codebase's supplement-guidance rules must check these factors, not just give a generic mg/kg number.
